standard_prerequisites.name: The diagonal morphism is an immersion, so that it has an ideal sheaf on an open subscheme of the fibre product containing its image; the author invokes the same-chapter statement for this and for the shape of the chosen open

standard_prerequisites.name: The conormal sheaf of an immersion, its definition, and its description over an affine chart as I/I^2, together with the affine description of the module of differentials
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Definition and lemmas of the same chapter cited at proof lines 6526-6528 and 6572-6576
standard_prerequisites.use: Names the target of the canonical map and lets the affine computation identify both sides with J/J^2 and with the module of differentials of the coordinate ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: The double-structure mechanism: a ring surjection A to B carrying two sections gives a derivation B to the kernel of the surjection, and the universal property of the module of differentials turns it into a linear map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited as an external chapter lemma at proof lines 6530 and 6540, and applied to the square-zero thickening O_W/J^2 at proof lines 6540-6548
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the canonical map from the module of differentials to the conormal sheaf.

core_obligations: Global construction of the conormal side: using that the diagonal is an immersion with ideal sheaf J on an open W, form the short exact sequence with kernel J/J^2 and cokernel the diagonal pushforward of O_X, and push it forward along the diagonal to present the conormal sheaf as the kernel of O_W/J^2 after inversion of the diagonal (proof lines 6515-6530).

Produce the derivation: the two projections of the fibre product give ring maps into O_W/J^2 whose pullbacks along the diagonal are two sections s_1 and s_2 of the surjection onto O_X; their difference is an S-derivation from O_X into the conormal sheaf (proof lines 6531-6542).

Apply the universal property of the module of relative differentials to obtain the canonical O_X-linear map from the sheaf of differentials to the conormal sheaf of the diagonal, sending f dg to f s_2(g) minus f s_1(g) (proof lines 6543-6548).

Show the canonical map is an isomorphism by descending to affine charts: for affine opens U = Spec(A) mapping into Spec(R), identify U times_V U with Spec(A tensor_R A), the ideal sheaf with the kernel J of the multiplication A tensor_R A to A, the conormal sheaf with J/J^2 and the differentials with those of A over R, so that the canonical map becomes a db to a tensor b minus ab tensor 1, which the author identifies as an isomorphism by the cited algebra statement (proof lines 6549-6593).
proof_roadmap: Build the canonical map globally from the square-zero thickening of the diagonal and the two sections coming from the projections (proof lines 6513-6548).

Check that the map is an isomorphism chart by chart over affine opens, where both sides become J/J^2 and the module of differentials of a tensor product algebra and the map is an explicit formula (proof lines 6549-6593).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the canonical identification of the sheaf of relative differentials of f : X to S with the conormal sheaf of the diagonal immersion X to X times_S X (statement lines 6506-6511). The counted proof does two genuinely different things: it constructs the canonical map globally, by forming the square-zero thickening of the diagonal, exhibiting the conormal sheaf as the kernel of the resulting surjection, and then manufacturing the derivation as the difference of the two sections induced by the projections, which invokes the universal property of the module of differentials (proof lines 6515-6548); and it verifies the isomorphism over an affine chart U = Spec(A) over Spec(R), where the conormal sheaf becomes J/J^2 for the kernel of the multiplication of the tensor product algebra and the canonical map becomes the explicit formula sending a db to a tensor b minus ab tensor 1 (proof lines 6549-6593). It is H2: the final identification of the explicit formula is delegated to a cited algebra statement, but the construction of the map and the affine reduction are the author's own and are carried out in the counted span.
